dedupe_keys.name: florida waste management system capacity analysis 2025

description: This report estimates the capacity of Florida's solid waste disposal and processing facilities and how long it will last as the population grows. It was written for the Florida Department of Environmental Protection by researchers at the University of Florida, Florida Polytechnic University and Florida Atlantic University under the Solid Waste Infrastructure for Recycling grant, and was completed in May 2025. It covers Class I landfills, waste-to-energy plants, ash monofills, yard trash disposal, materials recovery facilities and organics processing, using publicly reported data, conversations with operators and historic disposal and recycling trends. Key figures: 39 active Class I landfills received about 20.9 million tons in 2023 and had about 470.2 million tons of permitted and 164.1 million tons of constructed airspace left on 1 January 2025; nine waste-to-energy plants designed for about 6 million tons a year operate closer to 5.5 million tons. The report is a free PDF with facility tables; no licence is stated. Caveats: estimates carry uncertainty from reported data, and trends do not anticipate disasters or pandemics. Simulation uses: facility capacities and remaining airspace for waste network, debris management and capacity planning models in Florida. Related records: the EPA Disaster Debris Recovery Tool (data-epa-disaster-debris-recovery-tool) locates landfills and recyclers for disaster debris.
